name: Streaming Algorithms & Digital Audio
description: Questions covering: Audio Interfaces, Sound Recording, Data Storage, Internet Protocols...

questions.question: Which industry standard for connecting electronic musical instruments was originally co-developed by manufacturers like Roland and Sequential Circuits in the early 1980s?
questions.explanation_correct: MIDI (Musical Instrument Digital Interface) carries performance and control messages between instruments and computers; its development involved several manufacturers.
questions.explanation_incorrect: These options include balanced audio connectors (XLR), general data ports (USB-C), or professional digital audio transfer protocols (AES/EBU).

questions.question: What microphone recording technique is designed to replicate the human auditory system by capturing spatial depth?
questions.explanation_correct: Binaural recording typically uses microphones near the ears, sometimes in a dummy head, to capture cues that can create spatial perception, especially over headphones.
questions.explanation_incorrect: XY, ORTF and Mid-Side are other stereo recording arrangements; ORTF also uses microphone spacing to capture spatial information.

questions.question: Which digital medium, first released in 1982, established the early standard for consumer optical disc audio?
questions.explanation_correct: The Compact Disc launched in 1982 and became a major consumer optical audio medium using PCM.
questions.explanation_incorrect: These alternative formats were introduced later and utilize higher storage capacities or different encoding standards.

questions.question: What does the acronym RTSP stand for in media streaming?
questions.explanation_correct: RTSP stands for Real Time Streaming Protocol; it controls media sessions, including playback operations.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other phrases are not expansions of RTSP.

questions.question: Which audio processor reduces a signal’s level above a set threshold according to a compression ratio?
questions.explanation_correct: A compressor reduces dynamic range by applying gain reduction above its threshold. A limiter is a related form of compression, often with a high ratio.
questions.explanation_incorrect: An expander, high-pass filter and panner perform different processing functions.

questions.question: What process is used to reduce or eliminate unwanted constant spectral elements like tape hiss from audio recordings?
questions.explanation_correct: Noise reduction can estimate and suppress unwanted background noise such as hiss. Results depend on the signal and processing and may introduce artifacts.
questions.explanation_incorrect: These processes manipulate tone, amplitude, or bit representation without specifically targeting background noise floor reduction.

questions.question: Which network delivery method transmits a single stream to a group of destination computers simultaneously?
questions.explanation_correct: Multicast addresses a selected group of receivers; network equipment can replicate packets along paths to group members.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Unicast addresses one destination, broadcast addresses all hosts in a broadcast domain, and anycast routes to one of several eligible destinations.

questions.question: Which type of digital filter is characterized by a response that settles to zero in a finite number of sampling intervals?
questions.explanation_correct: FIR means finite impulse response: for a finite-length FIR filter, the response to an impulse ends after a finite number of samples.
questions.explanation_incorrect: IIR denotes infinite impulse response; microphones and loudspeakers are transducers.

questions.question: What does AAC stand for in digital audio coding?
questions.explanation_correct: AAC stands for Advanced Audio Coding, a family of lossy audio coding formats used in many media services.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other phrases are not expansions of AAC.

questions.question: What is the common term for the ratio of the desired audio signal power level to the unintended interference power level?
questions.explanation_correct: Signal-to-noise ratio compares signal power with noise power, often expressed in decibels.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Dynamic range, distortion and sample rate describe different aspects of a system.

questions.question: What physical high-definition audio format was co-developed by Sony and Philips to offer DSD audio?
questions.explanation_correct: Super Audio CD (SACD), developed by Sony and Philips, uses Direct Stream Digital encoding. Audible fidelity also depends on the recording, mastering and playback chain.
questions.explanation_incorrect: These other formats are either based on PCM encoding or represent different generations of optical storage technology.

questions.question: What term describes the continuous transmission of audio data allowing playback before the entire file is downloaded?
questions.explanation_correct: Streaming allows playback as media data arrives, without requiring the complete file first. Players commonly buffer some data.
questions.explanation_incorrect: These terms describe the intermediate storage or the full retrieval process rather than the continuous delivery method.

questions.question: Which type of compression reduces data size by discarding information and cannot generally reconstruct the original bit-for-bit?
questions.explanation_correct: Lossy compression discards or approximates information. Encoders may use psychoacoustic models, but compression artifacts can be audible.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Lossless compression permits exact reconstruction of the original data.

questions.question: Which metric measures the total amount of time it takes to send a data packet from client to server and receive an acknowledgment?
questions.explanation_correct: RTT measures the complete transit time for a packet travel cycle in a network connection.
questions.explanation_incorrect: These are related network variables but do not specifically measure the full client-server transit verification cycle.

questions.question: What parameter determines the range of amplitude resolution assigned to each individual digital audio sample?
questions.explanation_correct: In integer PCM, bit depth determines the number of available amplitude levels and affects quantization noise and theoretical dynamic range.
questions.explanation_incorrect: These metrics concern the temporal resolution or frequency range rather than the amplitude precision per sample.

questions.question: Which popular streaming platform is recognized for employing a proprietary recommendation engine known for its 'Discover Weekly' feature?
questions.explanation_correct: Discover Weekly is a Spotify playlist feature that uses listening-related signals and recommendation methods.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Tidal, Pandora and Apple Music are separate services with their own recommendation features.

questions.question: Which Linux sound server was widely used before PipeWire became a common alternative?
questions.explanation_correct: PulseAudio is a Linux sound server. PipeWire can also provide a PulseAudio-compatible server and is used on many systems.
questions.explanation_incorrect: DirectSound, ASIO and CoreAudio are different audio APIs or driver interfaces, mainly associated with Windows or macOS.

questions.question: What is the fundamental digital process of mathematically aggregating multiple audio tracks into a single stream?
questions.explanation_correct: Digital summing adds corresponding sample values from multiple signals, typically with gain management to avoid overload.
questions.explanation_incorrect: These terms refer to gain adjustment, bit-rounding, or the digital translation process, not the combining of tracks.

questions.question: Which Bluetooth audio codec family is associated with Qualcomm?
questions.explanation_correct: aptX is a family of Bluetooth audio codecs associated with Qualcomm. Actual quality depends on codec variant, settings and devices.
questions.explanation_incorrect: FLAC is a lossless codec; WAV and AIFF are audio file containers.

questions.question: What digital effect simulates the sound reflection characteristics of a physical space?
questions.explanation_correct: Reverberation consists of many reflections that persist after a sound; digital reverb can simulate characteristics of physical or imagined spaces.
questions.explanation_incorrect: These other effects create time-based repetitions or frequency modulations rather than spatial room reflection patterns.

questions.question: Which audio processor component attenuates frequencies above a defined threshold while allowing lower frequencies to pass?
questions.explanation_correct: A low-pass filter passes lower frequencies and attenuates higher frequencies, with a transition around the cutoff rather than an ideal abrupt boundary.
questions.explanation_incorrect: High-pass, band-pass, and notch filters perform different operations on the frequency spectrum, such as cutting lows or isolating specific regions.

questions.question: What is the standard method used to convert analog signals into digital data by sampling pulse amplitudes?
questions.explanation_correct: Pulse-Code Modulation (PCM) represents sampled analog signals as a sequence of binary values.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Other options describe different techniques for modulation, switching, or signal representation in electrical engineering.

questions.question: Which professional digital audio interface standard was developed to transmit two channels of audio over a single twisted-pair cable?
questions.explanation_correct: AES3 is a professional digital audio interface standard commonly used for two-channel audio over balanced twisted-pair cabling.
questions.explanation_incorrect: S/PDIF, ADAT and MADI use other specifications and can use different electrical or optical connections.

questions.question: What does the abbreviation bps mean when describing a digital data rate?
questions.explanation_correct: bps means bits per second, a unit of data rate. Bytes per second is another valid rate unit but uses bytes rather than bits.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other phrases do not expand bps.

questions.question: Which digital rights management system is provided by Google and used by Chrome and many streaming services?
questions.explanation_correct: Widevine is Google’s DRM system, supported by Chrome and used by numerous content providers.
questions.explanation_incorrect: FairPlay and PlayReady are DRM systems associated with Apple and Microsoft respectively.

questions.question: What is the name of the lossless audio compression format developed and utilized primarily within the Apple ecosystem?
questions.explanation_correct: ALAC stands for Apple Lossless Audio Codec. Apple developed it and published an open-source implementation; it compresses supported audio without loss.
questions.explanation_incorrect: FLAC, APE, and WavPack are also lossless codecs but operate under different technical specifications and ownership structures.

questions.question: What term describes the phenomenon where frequencies higher than half the sampling rate are misinterpreted as lower frequencies during digital conversion?
questions.explanation_correct: Aliasing occurs when distinct continuous-time frequencies become indistinguishable after sampling. Anti-alias filtering helps limit it.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Jitter relates to timing errors, quantization describes rounding errors, and ghosting is typically a visual artifact.

questions.question: Which specific metadata standard is employed to embed artist, album, and track information within the frame of an MP3 file?
questions.explanation_correct: ID3 is a tagging format commonly used to store metadata such as artist, title and album in MP3 files.
questions.explanation_incorrect: EXIF and IPTC are frequently associated with images; XMP is a metadata framework used across several media types.

questions.question: In the context of video streaming, what is the architectural model where the client initiates requests to retrieve individual segments from a server?
questions.explanation_correct: In pull-based delivery such as typical HLS or DASH, the player requests media resources or segments from a server.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Push-based describes a different initiation model; unicast and multicast describe addressing rather than whether delivery is pull-based.

questions.question: What error correction coding scheme was standard on Compact Discs to recover missing data due to surface damage?
questions.explanation_correct: Reed-Solomon codes were chosen for CDs due to their efficiency in correcting burst errors caused by physical debris on the disc.
questions.explanation_incorrect: While Hamming, Turbo, and LDPC are error-correcting codes, they serve different primary use cases in telecommunications and data storage.

questions.question: What broad term describes audio presentation intended to create a sense of sound sources around a listener?
questions.explanation_correct: Spatial audio is a broad term for techniques that create perceived sound position. Binaural, channel-based and object-based methods may be used.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Quantization, dithering and normalization are different audio-processing operations.

questions.question: In digital audio systems, what term identifies the time interval between the entry of a signal and its subsequent output?
questions.explanation_correct: Latency measures the delay inherent in signal processing, which is critical for real-time applications.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Throughput is a transfer rate, jitter is timing variation, and buffer size can affect but is not itself a measurement of end-to-end latency.

questions.question: Which multimedia container was developed and is maintained by the Xiph.Org Foundation?
questions.explanation_correct: Ogg is an open multimedia container developed by Xiph.Org; it can carry codecs including Vorbis and Opus.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Matroska, WebM and MP4 are other multimedia container formats.

questions.question: What is the technical term for the unwanted variation or oscillation in the timing of clock pulses in digital data transmission?
questions.explanation_correct: Jitter represents the short-term deviation from the ideal timing of a digital signal's clock pulses.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Drift is a long-term deviation, latency is a delay, and skew refers to signal timing differences between parallel lines.

questions.question: Which transport protocol is used in some low-latency interactive streams and does not itself guarantee delivery or ordering?
questions.explanation_correct: UDP is a transport protocol that does not itself guarantee delivery or order. Applications can add their own recovery mechanisms.
questions.explanation_incorrect: TCP and SCTP provide transport-level reliability mechanisms; HTTP is an application-layer protocol.

questions.question: What is the term for a specific compression artifact where faint sounds appear immediately before a sharp attack transient?
questions.explanation_correct: Pre-echo occurs when quantization noise is smeared backward in time due to block-based processing in psychoacoustic codecs.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Quantization noise, aliasing, and filtering are general terms and do not specifically describe this temporal artifact.

questions.question: What acronym refers to software applications designed specifically for recording, editing, and producing digital audio?
questions.explanation_correct: A digital audio workstation (DAW) is software for recording, arranging, editing or producing audio.
questions.explanation_incorrect: An IDE supports software development, NLE usually refers to non-linear editing, and VST is a plugin technology.

questions.question: What process scales an audio file uniformly so its highest peak reaches a specified target level?
questions.explanation_correct: Peak normalization scales the signal to a target peak. The target can be below 0 dBFS, and this differs from loudness normalization.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Dithering adds low-level noise to mask rounding errors, quantization is the bit-depth assignment, and resampling changes the sample rate.

questions.question: What technique involves re-encoding a digital stream from one bitrate or format to another to ensure wider device compatibility?
questions.explanation_correct: Transcoding converts media from one encoding to another and may involve decoding followed by re-encoding.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options describe recording setup or musical notation rather than encoded-media conversion.

questions.question: Which psychoacoustic concept defines the smallest change in a signal that a human ear can reliably perceive?
questions.explanation_correct: A just noticeable difference is the smallest change in a parameter detected under specified conditions; it depends on the listener and test.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Absolute threshold, critical bands, and masking are other psychoacoustic phenomena distinct from the measurement of perceptual thresholds.

questions.question: Which term describes the perceived highness or lowness of a sound?
questions.explanation_correct: Pitch is a perceptual property often associated with frequency or periodicity, though the relationship is not always one-to-one.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Timbre describes the tone quality, amplitude relates to loudness, and resonance is a physical amplification phenomenon.

questions.question: What processing technique changes audio duration while aiming to preserve its perceived pitch?
questions.explanation_correct: Time stretching changes duration independently of perceived pitch, though processing may introduce audible artifacts.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Pitch shifting changes perceived pitch; normalization changes gain and quantization maps amplitudes to discrete levels.

questions.question: Which audio codec was developed by the Xiph.Org Foundation as a free, open-source replacement for proprietary formats?
questions.explanation_correct: Vorbis is an open lossy audio coding format developed by Xiph.Org.
questions.explanation_incorrect: AAC, MP3 and ATRAC are other audio coding formats with different histories and licensing.

questions.question: Which streaming server project is associated with Xiph.Org?
questions.explanation_correct: Icecast is specifically designed for streaming audio and media in real-time to multiple clients.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Apache and Nginx are general web servers that can also serve media; MySQL is a database management system.

questions.question: Which technology enables the delivery of voice communications and multimedia sessions over Internet Protocol networks?
questions.explanation_correct: Voice over IP (VoIP) carries voice using Internet Protocol networks, usually as encoded digital audio packets.
questions.explanation_incorrect: DSL refers to broadband access, ATM is a network technology, and PSTN is the traditional circuit-switched telephone network.

questions.question: What visual representation displays the frequency spectrum of a signal as it varies over the course of time?
questions.explanation_correct: A spectrogram visually maps signal intensity across frequency and time coordinates.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Oscilloscopes show voltage over time, vectorscopes map phase relationships, and Lissajous curves visualize signal phase differences.

questions.question: Which object-based immersive audio format is developed by Dolby?
questions.explanation_correct: Dolby Atmos can combine channel-based beds with audio objects and metadata to render sound in a suitable playback setup.
questions.explanation_incorrect: DTS:X is also an object-based immersive format; stereo and quadraphonic refer to channel arrangements.

questions.question: Which digital radio family, including DAB+, is used in many European countries?
questions.explanation_correct: DAB and DAB+ are digital radio broadcasting standards used in a number of European markets; deployment differs by country.
questions.explanation_incorrect: HD Radio is used primarily in North America, AM is an analog broadcast mode, and SiriusXM is a proprietary satellite service.

questions.question: Which proprietary audio coder format was developed by Microsoft for use within the Windows Media framework?
questions.explanation_correct: Windows Media Audio (WMA) is a series of codecs developed by Microsoft.
questions.explanation_incorrect: ALAC and FLAC are lossless formats, and OGG is an open-source container format.

questions.question: What phenomenon occurs when one or more digital data packets fail to reach their intended destination during a network stream?
questions.explanation_correct: Packet loss occurs when packets fail to reach their destination. Depending on the protocol and application, losses can cause artifacts or be recovered.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Latency measures delay, jitter is the variation in delay, and throughput relates to total data transfer capacity.

questions.question: Which type of electronic signal processing circuit allows frequencies within a specific range to pass, while rejecting frequencies outside that range?
questions.explanation_correct: A band-pass filter passes a selected range of frequencies while attenuating frequencies outside it; real filters have transition bands.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Low-pass and high-pass filters only block one end of the spectrum, while notch filters remove a narrow frequency band.

questions.question: What feature allows for a smooth transition where the volume of one audio track fades out while another simultaneously fades in?
questions.explanation_correct: A crossfade overlaps a fade-out and fade-in. It can smooth a transition between tracks or clips.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Normalization alters overall gain, clipping is digital distortion, and compression reduces dynamic range.

questions.question: Which protocol is the standard for transmitting encrypted data safely across computer networks for media streaming?
questions.explanation_correct: HTTPS uses TLS to protect HTTP traffic in transit. Security also depends on correct configuration and endpoint behavior.
questions.explanation_incorrect: HTTP is unencrypted, FTP is for file transfers, and Telnet is an insecure remote login protocol.

questions.question: What process involves the automatic transformation of written character input into synthesized audible speech output?
questions.explanation_correct: Text-to-Speech (TTS) utilizes linguistic analysis and signal processing to convert text into artificial human speech.
questions.explanation_incorrect: ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition) is the reverse process, OCR converts images to text, and PCM is an audio storage format.

questions.question: What specific data structure is frequently used as a buffer to handle continuous, real-time flows of streaming audio data?
questions.explanation_correct: A circular buffer uses a fixed-size region with wraparound read and write positions. Its behavior on overflow depends on the implementation.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Stacks, linked lists and trees have different structures, though many data structures can support queues or buffering.

questions.question: Which professional digital multi-channel audio connection protocol was originally developed by Alesis for studio equipment?
questions.explanation_correct: ADAT Lightpipe is an optical digital audio interface associated with Alesis. A standard single link carries eight channels at 44.1 or 48 kHz; higher rates use different channel arrangements.
questions.explanation_incorrect: AES3 and SPDIF are stereo standards, and USB is a general-purpose data bus.

questions.question: What is the standard unit of measurement used in modern digital audio to quantify perceived loudness rather than raw peak signal amplitude?
questions.explanation_correct: LUFS expresses measured loudness relative to full scale, using standardized weighting and integration intended to better reflect perceived loudness.
questions.explanation_incorrect: dBFS measures digital level relative to full scale, SPL measures sound pressure level, and RMS describes a mathematical level measure.

questions.question: Which XML-based feed format is commonly used to distribute podcast episode metadata and links?
questions.explanation_correct: RSS feeds are widely used to publish podcast metadata and links to episodes; distribution methods can vary.
questions.explanation_incorrect: JSON, HTML, and YAML are data serialization or markup formats not typically used for feed syndication standards.

questions.question: What category of audio synthesis creates sounds by mathematically modeling the physical properties of musical instruments?
questions.explanation_correct: Physical modeling simulates the real-world physics of an instrument, such as vibrating strings or air columns.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Subtractive, additive, and granular synthesis manipulate wave components rather than mimicking physical mechanics.

questions.question: What audio phenomenon occurs when the peak of one sound wave coincides with the trough of another, resulting in signal cancellation?
questions.explanation_correct: When aligned waveforms combine with opposite phase, destructive interference can reduce their sum. Exact cancellation depends on amplitude and timing.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Harmonic distortion adds frequency artifacts, aliasing is a sampling error, and quantization error occurs in binary conversion.

questions.question: Which audio codec was specifically designed for efficient speech compression in voice applications?
questions.explanation_correct: Speex is an open-source lossy codec designed especially for speech.
questions.explanation_incorrect: FLAC is lossless; MP3 and AAC are general-purpose lossy formats that can also encode speech.

questions.question: What is the standard bit depth utilized for recording and playback of commercial audio compact discs?
questions.explanation_correct: Red Book standard audio CDs utilize a 16-bit depth per sample at a 44.1 kHz sampling rate.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Other bit depths like 8-bit, 12-bit, or 24-bit are used in different technical contexts or high-resolution formats, not the CD standard.

questions.question: Which encoding approach adjusts the data rate dynamically depending on the complexity of the signal segment?
questions.explanation_correct: VBR varies the number of bits over time, often allocating more to difficult passages. Actual quality and allocation depend on the codec and settings.
questions.explanation_incorrect: CBR aims for a fixed rate; lossless codecs can also produce variable bitrates.

questions.question: What JavaScript standard interface allows developers to process and synthesize audio within a browser?
questions.explanation_correct: The Web Audio API provides a powerful and versatile system for controlling audio on the web.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Canvas, WebGL, and Gamepad are APIs designed for graphics and input rather than audio processing.

questions.question: Which audio driver interface was specified by Steinberg to support low-latency audio on computers?
questions.explanation_correct: ASIO is a driver interface developed by Steinberg for low-latency audio access. Latency depends on the driver, hardware and buffer settings.
questions.explanation_incorrect: DirectSound, MME and WDM are other Windows audio interfaces or driver-model terms with different roles.

questions.question: In a live streaming architecture, which component is responsible for retrieving and delivering the source stream content?
questions.explanation_correct: An origin server is the authoritative source from which distribution components retrieve media. Caches and proxies may deliver copies to clients.
questions.explanation_incorrect: A client cache or proxy may also deliver content, but it is not necessarily the authoritative origin.

questions.question: Which proprietary lossy audio codec was developed by Sony for use in MiniDisc players?
questions.explanation_correct: ATRAC (Adaptive TRansform Acoustic Coding) is a family of proprietary audio compression algorithms developed by Sony.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Ogg Vorbis, WMA, and Opus are alternative codecs developed by different entities and were not the primary format for early MiniDisc hardware.

questions.question: Which technique uses oversampling and noise shaping to represent signals with a high-rate, low-bit-depth stream?
questions.explanation_correct: Delta-sigma modulation combines oversampling and noise shaping and is used in converters and formats such as DSD.
questions.explanation_incorrect: PWM, FM and phase modulation encode information differently.

questions.question: Which international identifier is assigned to a particular sound recording or music video?
questions.explanation_correct: ISRC stands for International Standard Recording Code and identifies recordings, not the underlying composition itself.
questions.explanation_incorrect: ISBN and ISSN identify books and serial publications; DOI is a broader digital object identifier.

questions.question: What type of filter is characterized by having feedback, resulting in a theoretically infinite impulse response?
questions.explanation_correct: An IIR filter has an impulse response of theoretically infinite duration; feedback is a common way to implement it.
questions.explanation_incorrect: An FIR filter has a finite impulse response; microphones and oscilloscopes are devices rather than filter response classes.

questions.question: Which technology enables real-time peer-to-peer communication through web browsers without requiring plugins?
questions.explanation_correct: WebRTC provides browsers and mobile applications with real-time communication capabilities via simple APIs.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Flash, Silverlight, and Java Applets are legacy technologies that often required external browser plugins to function.

questions.question: Which audio container format was primarily developed by Apple for Mac-based digital audio storage?
questions.explanation_correct: AIFF is an audio file format developed by Apple; it commonly carries uncompressed PCM but can also support other encodings.
questions.explanation_incorrect: WAV is another audio container; Ogg and FLAC are different formats or codecs.

questions.question: Which logarithmic unit is used to express an audio level relative to a specified reference?
questions.explanation_correct: The decibel expresses a logarithmic ratio. An audio level such as dB SPL or dBFS must specify its reference.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Hertz measures frequency, volts electric potential and pascals pressure; these are not logarithmic level units.

questions.question: Which audio-over-IP networking system carries multichannel digital audio over compatible Ethernet networks?
questions.explanation_correct: Dante is an audio-over-IP system that can carry multichannel digital audio over compatible IP networks; configuration and capabilities depend on devices.
questions.explanation_incorrect: MIDI is a control protocol; USB and FireWire are peripheral data buses, not network audio protocols for Ethernet.

questions.question: Which audio processor is commonly used to restrict signal peaks near a chosen level?
questions.explanation_correct: A limiter applies strong gain reduction to restrict peaks. Its effectiveness depends on settings and implementation, including true-peak handling; no device guarantees all distortion is prevented.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Expanders and gates affect the low end or quiet sections, while equalizers modify frequency content rather than preventing clipping.

questions.question: What is the process of conveying data or information by converting it into non-speech sound?
questions.explanation_correct: Sonification is the use of non-speech audio to convey information or perceptualize data.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Digitization, sampling, and normalization relate to recording and processing methods rather than data-to-sound translation.

questions.question: Which streaming method dynamically adjusts bitrate during playback to match current network conditions?
questions.explanation_correct: Adaptive bitrate streaming can switch among encoded variants in response to conditions. It can reduce interruptions but cannot guarantee uninterrupted playback.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Unicast and multicast describe addressing, while progressive download describes another delivery approach.

questions.question: Which label is commonly used for audio distributed at a higher sample rate or bit depth than standard CD audio?
questions.explanation_correct: Hi-Res Audio commonly refers to audio specifications above CD resolution. Higher numerical resolution alone does not guarantee better audible quality.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Lo-fi, mono and voice-grade describe different properties and do not specify higher-than-CD resolution.

questions.question: Which format represents raw digital audio data with no compression applied to the sample stream?
questions.explanation_correct: LPCM (Linear Pulse Code Modulation) is the standard method for encoding uncompressed digital audio.
questions.explanation_incorrect: AAC, MP3, and Vorbis are all lossy, compressed audio codecs, not raw uncompressed data streams.

questions.question: Which mathematical technique models the human vocal tract to efficiently represent speech as digital parameters?
questions.explanation_correct: Linear Predictive Coding (LPC) estimates parameters of a linear system to model the production of human speech.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Fourier and wavelets are mathematical transformations, and PCM is an encoding method, but none specifically model the vocal tract like LPC.

questions.question: Which lossless audio codec is maintained as part of the Xiph.Org project?
questions.explanation_correct: FLAC, the Free Lossless Audio Codec, was originally created by Josh Coalson and became a Xiph.Org project.
questions.explanation_incorrect: ALAC is an Apple-developed lossless codec; WAV and AIFF are audio containers.

questions.question: Which protocol is primarily designed for the real-time transport of audio and video over IP networks?
questions.explanation_correct: RTP provides a framework for transporting real-time audio and video over IP. Applications often combine it with other protocols.
questions.explanation_incorrect: HTTP is for web resource fetching, FTP is for file transfers, and SMTP is for email.

questions.question: What is the process of adding low-level noise to a digital audio file to reduce quantization distortion when decreasing bit depth?
questions.explanation_correct: Dither adds carefully controlled noise before quantization to reduce signal-correlated quantization distortion, trading it for a noise floor.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Normalization changes gain, while compression and limiting change dynamics.

questions.question: What does MP3 stand for in the original MPEG-1 audio standard?
questions.explanation_correct: MP3 denotes MPEG-1 Audio Layer III; related MPEG-2 extensions also use the MP3 name.
questions.explanation_incorrect: AAC-LC, HE-AAC and AC-3 denote different audio coding formats.

questions.question: What kind of distributed server system is used to deliver content globally to users based on their geographic location?
questions.explanation_correct: A CDN distributes content through geographically distributed servers; routing may consider location, network conditions and server availability.
questions.explanation_incorrect: VPN, NAS, and LAN refer to networking and storage architectures, not global content distribution strategies.

questions.question: What algorithm efficiently computes the discrete Fourier transform of a sequence?
questions.explanation_correct: The fast Fourier transform (FFT) is a family of algorithms for efficiently computing a discrete Fourier transform.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Cosine, wavelet and Laplace transforms are other mathematical tools rather than the FFT definition.

questions.question: Which open standard did the MPEG committee develop to facilitate adaptive bitrate streaming over HTTP?
questions.explanation_correct: MPEG-DASH is the international standard for Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP.
questions.explanation_incorrect: HLS is another HTTP-based adaptive streaming protocol, documented in an IETF RFC; RTMP and RTSP serve different streaming functions.

questions.question: Which open-source audio codec, standardized by the IETF, is optimized for high-quality, low-latency communication over the internet?
questions.explanation_correct: Opus was developed collaboratively, including contributions from Xiph.Org and Skype, and standardized by the IETF for interactive speech and audio.
questions.explanation_incorrect: FLAC, linear PCM and DSD are different formats; Opus is the IETF-standardized interactive codec in this list.

questions.question: What is the name for twice the highest frequency in an ideal real-valued baseband signal?
questions.explanation_correct: The Nyquist rate is twice the highest frequency in an ideal band-limited baseband signal. Practical sampling needs suitable anti-alias filtering and margin.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Bit depth describes quantization resolution; volume and clock drift are different concepts.

questions.question: Which consumer-grade digital audio interface protocol is commonly used to transmit data over coaxial or TOSLINK optical cables?
questions.explanation_correct: S/PDIF is a consumer digital audio interface commonly carried over coaxial RCA or optical TOSLINK connections.
questions.explanation_incorrect: AES3 is commonly used professionally; I²C and GPIO serve different hardware-interface functions.

questions.question: Which proprietary protocol is used by Apple devices for wireless streaming of audio and video?
questions.explanation_correct: AirPlay is Apple's trademarked suite of protocols for streaming video and audio between devices.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Miracast, Chromecast, and DLNA are technologies from other developers for media streaming.

questions.question: Which protocol, first developed by Macromedia and later associated with Adobe Flash, carried streaming media to Flash players?
questions.explanation_correct: RTMP was developed by Macromedia, later acquired by Adobe, and became associated with Flash media streaming.
questions.explanation_incorrect: HLS and DASH are HTTP-based streaming formats; RTP is a real-time transport protocol.

questions.question: In psychoacoustics, what is the term for when a louder sound prevents the human ear from perceiving a quieter, simultaneous sound?
questions.explanation_correct: Auditory masking describes the phenomenon where one sound partially or completely obscures another.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other phenomena are interference or spatial effects, not related to the psychology of hearing.

questions.question: Which lossy audio codec remains widely prevalent in traditional telecommunications due to its simplicity and low processing overhead?
questions.explanation_correct: G.711 is a narrowband speech coding standard widely used in telephony, using logarithmic PCM companding.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other formats are modern high-quality codecs; G.711 is notable for its simplicity in digital telephony.

questions.question: Which container format is the standard for uncompressed audio on the Windows platform?
questions.explanation_correct: WAV is a container commonly used for PCM audio on Windows; it can also hold other audio encodings.
questions.explanation_incorrect: MP3 and AAC are lossy codecs; FLAC is a lossless codec.

questions.question: What is the common term for the distortion introduced by the process of mapping continuous values to discrete levels?
questions.explanation_correct: Quantization error is the difference between a value and its quantized representation. Modeling it as noise is useful in some, but not all, conditions.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other types of noise are physical or statistical noise models unrelated to digital conversion truncation.

questions.question: What network component is used to store incoming data packets to compensate for variations in arrival times during streaming?
questions.explanation_correct: A jitter buffer temporarily holds received packets to reduce the effects of variation in arrival time; excessive delay or loss can still affect playback.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Headers, latency, and clocks are elements of timing and data tracking, not the buffering mechanism itself.

questions.question: Which HTTP-based streaming protocol did Apple develop as a successor to their direct-stream methods?
questions.explanation_correct: HTTP Live Streaming (HLS) is an Apple-developed HTTP-based streaming protocol, publicly documented in RFC 8216.
questions.explanation_incorrect: MPEG-DASH is another HTTP-based adaptive streaming standard; RTMP and RTSP serve different roles.

questions.question: What hardware component is responsible for reconstructing an analog signal from a sequence of digital bits?
questions.explanation_correct: A DAC converts digital sample values into a corresponding analog electrical signal. Playback also depends on filtering and other hardware.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other devices are either for recording or modifying signal properties, not for playback output.

questions.question: What sound synthesis technique involves varying the frequency of an oscillator using a modulator signal?
questions.explanation_correct: FM synthesis varies an oscillator’s instantaneous frequency using a modulating signal, producing sidebands and changing timbre.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Additive, subtractive, and granular are different synthesis methods using summation, filtering, or grain manipulation.
